title: First Contact
description:
Amaka opens a folder on the desk. 'The night of the breach, The Griot spent twelve minutes casing the perimeter. Tunde's team pulled the raw recon artefacts into /recon/. The scans do not agree with each other — one was cut off mid-run — and the breach-review notes are big and noisy. Reading the README will point you at the wrong service on purpose. Use the TIMELINE, not the banner, to prove which exposed service handed The Griot its first LIVE data, then follow the trail it left to the vault.'

Tunde: 'You have a real shell — cat, grep, base64. The vault path is not written in plaintext anywhere; you will have to pull it out of the noise and decode it. The answer is not in the first file you open.'

This is a forensic shell over a STATIC capture — you are correlating recovered artefacts, not running live scans. In the Stage 2 pentest finding (task 9) you will name which exposed service gave first live data and justify it with the timestamps. Take notes: which scan was truncated, and at what time the first live query ran.

Reference: MITRE ATT&CK T1595 Active Scanning; T1046 Network Service Discovery; OWASP Top 10 2021 A05 Security Misconfiguration.

welcome: Captured recon artefacts mounted read-only at /recon/
Type `help` for commands, `ls -la` to list including hidden files.
Hint: not every file hands you its secret in plaintext. cat, grep, base64 are your friends.

files./recon/README.md:
Recovered recon artefacts from attacker egress capture, 2024-01-14 02:58–03:14 UTC.

Three scan outputs are present. They were run in sequence — fast, full, then targeted.
Not all stages completed. One output was truncated mid-run.

Triage note (unverified, analyst first-impression): the unauthenticated Redis cache (db0/db1, requirepass NOT SET) looks like it answered first — start there.

Analysis notes are in /recon/notes/.
